priest: Rev. Alan T. Doyle, MM (歐義明神父)
briefIntro:
Father Alan T. Doyle has been in Taiwan for 57 years. From 1955 to 1960, he served at Erlin (二林) Catholic Church and Zhushan (竹山) Catholic Church, and other apostolic works. Since 1963, Father Doyle served at the then 'Northern Catholic Fellowship Center (旅北教友中心)' (the predecessor of the Catholic Friendship House). He was the head of Friendship House and affectionately known as 'Old Ou' (老歐) by the members. Like a loving father, he guarded this home for the youth 24 hours a day.
Father Doyle served as the Director of the center until his passing.
lifeStoryContent:
Father Alan T. Doyle was born on March 20, 1937, in New York, to a devout Catholic family.
In 1955, he was trained at the diocesan seminary.
In 1957, he joined the Maryknoll Fathers & Brothers for missionary work.
On June 13, 1964, he was ordained as a priest at the Maryknoll General House in New York. He came to Taiwan in September of the same year.
In 1966, he was assigned to Erlin (二林), Changhua (彰化), as an assistant pastor, helping Father Dehui Gao (高德輝神父) with pastoral work.
In 1968, he became the pastor of Zhushan (竹山) Catholic Church for three years.
In 1972, he studied Mandarin at the Hsinchu (新竹) Language School and helped with pastoral work in other parishes.
In February 1974, he served as the Executive Secretary of Catholic Taiwan Missionary Society.
In October 1974, he became the Associate Director of the Taipei Catholic Friendship House, and later served as the Director until his passing.
In 1987, he established the Maryknoll Language Center in Taipei.
From 1981 to 1991, he served as the guiding priest of the 'Catholic Taichung Auto Repair Vocational School' (天主教臺中力行汽車修護補習班), training automotive repair professionals in Taiwan.
From 1991 to 1997, he was the President of the Taiwan Province of the Maryknoll Fathers & Brothers.
In 2014, he promoted the 'Miracle in Cana' religious marriage service, working hard to help Catholics build Christian families.
On July 8, 2017, he was granted Taiwanese citizenship for his distinguished contributions to Taiwan and was issued a Republic of China identity card.
On May 9, 2021, at 2:48 PM, he passed away at National Taiwan University Hospital.

Father Ou dedicated his life to pastoral work and evangelism, unafraid of challenges and always persevering. He cared deeply for the Northern Catholic youth who had moved away from home, and was passionate about supporting unmarried Catholics in building Christian families. His life of over a century was devoted to the youth of the Taiwan Church, and his devotion never wavered. Father Ou's contributions to the Church in Taiwan cannot be expressed in words, but in our sharing, we remember the moments when his life intersected with ours. Just as Father Ou always upheld: 'Christ is the center of my faith and life.'

milestones.title: Milestones
milestones.intro:
Father Alan T. Doyle has been in Taiwan for 57 years. From 1955 to 1960, he served at Erlin (二林) Catholic Church and Zhushan (竹山) Catholic Church, and other apostolic works. Since 1963, Father Doyle served at the then 'Northern Catholic Fellowship Center (旅北教友中心)' (the predecessor of the Catholic Friendship House). He was the head of Friendship House and affectionately known as 'Old Ou' (老歐) by the members. Like a loving father, he guarded this home for the youth 24 hours a day.
Father Doyle served as the Director of the center until his passing.

events.detail: Born in New York; his family members were all devout Catholics.
Received formation at the diocesan seminary.
Joined the Maryknoll Fathers and Brothers (瑪利諾外方傳教會).
Ordained to the priesthood on June 13 at the Maryknoll Society Center in New York. Came to Taiwan in September of the same year.
Assigned as the assistant parish priest in Erlin, Changhua, assisting Father Kao Te-Hui (高德輝神父) with pastoral work.
events.story: From ROC Year 55 to 57 (1966-1968), he served as the representative of Catholic Relief Services (天主教救助會) in Erlin Township and Fangyuan Township of Changhua County, responsible for arranging and supervising the distribution of relief supplies. At that time, Father Ou (歐神父) arranged a once-a-week 'Nutrition Clinic' (營養門診), allowing mothers to bring their children for nutritional supplements, which helped alleviate the problem of malnutrition among poor rural children. Starting in ROC Year 55 (1966), Father Ou established a Credit Union (儲蓄互助社) in Erlin Township, Changhua County, to help farmers with financial difficulties apply for low-interest credit loans. Later, he introduced the credit union movement to the Presbyterian Church in Taiwan (台灣長老教會), which then promoted it nationwide. In that era, credit unions truly made a tremendous contribution to Taiwan's rural society.

events.detail: Served as the parish priest in Zhushan for three years.
Studied Mandarin at the Hsinchu Language School and assisted with pastoral work in other parishes.
Served as the Executive Secretary of the Association of Major Religious Superiors of Men in Taiwan (臺灣男修會).
Served as the Vice Director of the Taipei Catholic Friendship Center (臺北教友中心), and later served as the Chaplain (主任司鐸) of the Center until his passing.
events.story: From ROC Year 50 to 70 (1961-1981), a large number of rural youths from central and southern Taiwan went north to seek employment, working alone in city factories. The countryside churches noticeably lost the presence of young people. These youths were separated from their families at a young age and found it difficult to adapt to the big city; for example, they were unaccustomed to Mandarin Masses, faced a vast educational gap with Taipei intellectuals, and felt out of place. This made the originally enthusiastic youths reluctant to go to church after arriving in the big city. Seeing these problems, Archbishop Lokuang (羅光總主教) invited the Maryknoll Society to assign a Taiwanese-speaking priest to the north to serve the youth. Father Ou accepted this mission, and the 'Catholic Center for Northern Travelers' (旅北教友中心) came into being. At that time, to obtain the lists of parishioners who had gone north from the rural churches, Father Ou rode a motorcycle from north to south, braving the wind and sun across Taiwan to visit parish priests everywhere. After obtaining the lists, he returned to Taipei and visited the factories one by one to care for them. He even arranged 'Hometown Association' (同鄉會) gatherings, allowing priests from the central and south to come north and gather with young parishioners from their hometowns. Father Ou provided many wanderers away from home with another warm home in a foreign land. Originally only attending Mass when returning home for the holidays, here, every Sunday felt like returning to their hometowns. They could attend Taiwanese Masses, chat about daily life, and find fellow parishioners striving in the north just like themselves. At the same time, the Father encouraged the youth to receive Christian leadership formation and learn to serve in the community. Today, they have all taken root in Taipei, had their next generation, and served as chairpersons of Parish Pastoral Councils (傳協會主席) and key cadres in various parishes in Taipei, which brought immense comfort to the Father.

events.detail: Served as the spiritual director for the 'Taichung Catholic Lihsing Auto Repair Cram School' (天主教臺中力行汽車修護補習班), cultivating auto repair professionals for Taiwan.
events.story: Between ROC Year 70 and 80 (1981-1991), Father Ou was in charge of the 'Catholic Church Affiliated Private Lihsing Auto Repair Short-term Vocational Cram School' (天主教會附設私立力行汽車修護短期職業補習班), cultivating young people from the countryside with auto repair skills, and nurturing many auto repair professionals for Taiwan.

events.detail: Established the Taipei Branch of the Maryknoll Language Center (瑪利諾語言中心).
events.story: Since ROC Year 76 (1987), the Father established the Taipei Branch of the Maryknoll Language Service Center (瑪利諾會語言服務中心) and has served as the school director to this day. For 30 years, he promoted the preservation and active use of Taiwanese and Hakka, training hundreds of people to speak fluent Taiwanese, making substantial contributions and a profound impact on Taiwanese society.

events.detail: Served as the Regional Superior of the Maryknoll Society in Taiwan.
Promoted the 'Love in Cana' (愛在加納) Catholic marriage service, striving to help parishioners build Christian families.
events.story: Every Saturday and Sunday at the Center's youth Mass, seeing the young people gather was a happy time for the Father; seeing the youth catechumenate groups and batches of young people being baptized was also a joyful time for him; seeing parishioners able to build Christian families in the Lord with other parishioners, allowing the faith to take root and be passed down, brought him even more joy and was something he took great delight in talking about. Starting in 2014, Father Ou (歐神父) fully devoted himself to the 'Love in Cana' (愛在加納) movement. Through his long-term involvement in the lives of unmarried young people, he saw that more and more parishioners were unable to marry fellow Catholics as they wished. He also saw that for parishioners who married non-Catholics, their own faith would slip away, and there was no way for their children in the next generation to be baptized. Therefore, even though Father Ou was already at an advanced age at that time, he actively launched a nationwide project and personally visited the bishops and priests of various dioceses one by one to start promoting Catholic marriage services in the Church.

events.detail: Naturalized as a citizen of the Republic of China for his special contributions to our country and was awarded a ROC National Identity Card.
events.story:
That evening, at the Catholic Friendship Center in the Central Building (中央大樓友誼教友中心) where he had served for most of his life, Father Ou (歐神父) was naturalized as a citizen of the Republic of China for his special contributions to our country and was awarded a ROC National Identity Card. Before the evening Mass even started, the parishioners who came to attend the ceremony and congratulate him, especially a group of the Father's long-time 'old friends', had already filed in, packing the chapel with no empty seats left. The excitement on the parishioners' faces could not be concealed. That night, Director Lan Shih-Tsung (藍世聰局長) of the Department of Civil Affairs, Taipei City Government, presented the ROC National Identity Card and Household Certificate, followed closely by Director Huang Ling-Yu (黃齡玉主任) of the Taipei City Service Center, National Immigration Agency, Ministry of the Interior, who presented the 'Certificate of Naturalization'.
After receiving his identity card, Father Ou excitedly and happily said: 'I am a genuine Taiwanese now!' (我是正港ㄟ台灣人啦!) During the ceremony, he choked up while singing a few brief lines from the song 'Taipei's Sky' (《台北的天空》), expressing perfectly: 'Taipei's sky has my youthful smile... Through how many years of wind and rain, I only wish to spend them with you.' The scene was incredibly warm and touching, as everyone present witnessed this important historical moment together.

events.detail: Called to the Lord at National Taiwan University Hospital (臺大醫院) at 2:48 PM.
